title: Food tests and chromatography; Eukaryotic cell ultrastructure
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE02a#t1 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t4 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t3 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM09a#N.4a, CE02a#N.8a, BM09a#N.14, CE02a#N.11a, CE02a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleolus
items.clue: Dense region that makes rRNA and assembles ribosomes

items.label: Reducing sugars
items.clue: Group made up of all monosaccharides plus maltose and lactose

items.label: Biuret test
items.clue: A change from blue to lilac shows that peptide bonds are present

items.label: Iodine test
items.clue: A change from orange-brown to blue-black shows that starch is present

questions.stem: A solution gives a negative result with iodine. With Benedict's reagent, heated, it stays blue. A fresh sample is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid, neutralised, and tested with Benedict's again: a brick-red precipitate forms. What does the solution contain?

options.text: A reducing sugar, because the final Benedict's test was positive.
Starch, which the acid broke down into glucose.
A non-reducing sugar, such as sucrose, and no reducing sugar.
A reducing sugar made by the acid joining smaller sugars by condensation.

questions.explanation: Negative first, positive after acid hydrolysis: the acid split a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a membrane-bound organelle of a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened sacs studded with ribosomes that synthesise proteins.
Mitochondria are bounded by a single membrane folded inward to form cristae.
Lysosomes are vesicles bounded by a single membrane that contain hydrolytic enzymes.
Secretory vesicles are lysosomes under another name, digesting worn-out organelles.

questions.explanation: Lysosomes are single-membrane sacs containing hydrolytic enzymes, kept separate from the rest of the cytoplasm, that digest material taken in and worn-out organelles.

questions.stem: A sample of milk is tested. Heated with Benedict's reagent: an orange-red precipitate. With biuret reagent: lilac. With iodine in potassium iodide: stays orange-brown. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: It contains glucose and no other sugar.
It contains starch, protein and a reducing sugar.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable lipid.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable starch.

questions.explanation: Precipitate: reducing sugar. Lilac: peptide bonds, so protein. No blue-black: no starch detected.

questions.stem: In an electron micrograph of an animal cell, a structure appears as a discrete stack of curved, flattened membrane sacs with small vesicles budding from its edges and no ribosomes attached. Which structure is it?

options.text: Golgi apparatus, where proteins are modified and packaged
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, where lipids are made
Mitochondrion, where aerobic cell respiration is carried out
Rough endoplasmic reticulum, where secreted proteins are made

questions.explanation: A stack of curved sacs, separate from the nuclear envelope, with no ribosomes and vesicles budding from its edges as proteins are packaged for transport.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph of a cell shows a large amount of rough ER, a large Golgi and many small vesicles close to the cell surface. What does this cell most likely do?

options.text: It makes large amounts of lipid, using the ribosomes on its ER.
It digests engulfed bacteria, using the enzymes in its many vesicles.
It makes proteins, such as enzymes, and releases them from the cell.
It makes proteins in the Golgi, which the ER then packs into vesicles.

questions.explanation: RER makes proteins; the Golgi modifies and packages them; vesicles carry them to the surface for release.
